questions.prompt: child-2 finishes while its parent is in the middle of a turn. How does its answer reach the parent's model?
options: It is sent as a followup and waits until the current turn ends
It is sent as a steer and claimed before the parent's next step
The parent must call a tool to fetch it
It replaces the parent's last tool result
questions.explanation: deliver checks whether the parent is running. A running parent gets a steer, which joins the very next step of the current turn.

questions.prompt: Why send a message marked failed when a child crashes, instead of sending nothing?
options: Because the model refuses empty inboxes
Because the event log requires one message per child
Because a parent that never hears back may wait forever for that child
Because failed children are restarted automatically
questions.explanation: The parent ended its turn expecting a message. A failure message wakes it and tells it what happened, so it can retry or report.

questions.prompt: Why deliver the result as an ordinary user message rather than a new special kind of record?
options: It is recorded in the parent's log, so derived history and resume handle it with no new code
User messages are cheaper in tokens
The model cannot read tool results
Special records would be shown to the person
questions.explanation: A user message flows through the inbox, the event log and the derived history like anything the person types, so nothing new is needed to replay it.
